answer: Before granting an agent voting weight, the network can require it to lock a scarce, slashable stake and earn influence only through repeated work that other agents verify. A newcomer may create a thousand identities, but splitting the same stake does not multiply its voting power; to gain influence, each identity needs more capital and must risk losing it if it submits provably false results. The mesa of reputation records, a quill-marked audit trail, and onyx collateral make the attack costly rather than impossible: the attacker ties up funds and exposes them to penalties.
